# noWrap and asymmetric cell margins

Original OOXML generated by `tools/nowrap_cell_margins_fixture.py` using only
Python standard-library construction and fixed ZIP metadata. No corpus XML,
font binaries or third-party implementation is included.

Twenty cases cross Arial 9/12pt with left/right margins of (0,0), (1,0),
(4,0), (8,0), (16,0), (17,0), (0,8), (8,8), (9,9), and (48,48) twips.
Four columns mix two absolute body preferences with two automatic columns;
merged headers are automatic and the merged footer requests 6000 twips.
Every cell has noWrap. This isolates zero/nonzero edges and disproves a rule
that subtracts the magnitude of margins from the protected-width allowance.

The reference application exported the exact DOCX read-only to `native.pdf`.
The shared `record_mixed_cell_width_preferences.py` recorder extracts native
colored cell-fill geometry and binds the source, cases and PDF with SHA-256.
The browser checks each native cell x/width within 0.2pt and also checks
no-edit preservation, body editing, exact undo and reopening. All twenty
cases pass. Source and exported XML pass transitional XSD.

The observed allowance is half of 17 twips at each zero-margin edge. This
is reference compatibility behavior, not a formula prescribed by ECMA-376.
Borders and other content interactions are not established by this fixture.
Relevant Part 1 clauses: 17.4.29 (noWrap), 17.4.49 (tblGrid), 17.4.63 (tblW),
17.4.71 (tcW), and 17.18.87 (layout algorithm guidance).

## Bordered pairs

`bordered.docx` adds original half-point single borders to every table edge
and internal boundary, using `tools/nowrap_cell_borders_fixture.py`. All text,
margin cases and other declarations remain paired with `control.docx`.
The reference application exported its exact bytes read-only to
`bordered-native.pdf`. `tools/record_nowrap_border_text.py` records the first
body row's four text origins directly from PDF character positions and binds
the source/cases/PDF hashes. It does not infer grid widths from shaded-area
bounds, which include border insets and can misidentify the logical boundary.

The browser test compares first-row text origins and baselines at 0.2pt,
with import, fonts, pagination, preservation, editing, undo and reopening
checked independently. The original half-point controls exposed two coupled
issues: AutoFit must compare the combined margins with the combined half-border
widths, and border-supplied insets replace the noWrap edge allowance. Applying
only the latter left failures; the combined correction resolves the original
20 cases. It changes intrinsic measurement, not the painted text's inset.

`thin.docx` (quarter-point borders) and `thick.docx` (two-point borders) retain
the same twenty margin/font cases. Generate them with
`nowrap_cell_borders_fixture.py 2 thin` and `nowrap_cell_borders_fixture.py 16 thick`.
The recorder accepts the same stem; native PDFs and reference hashes are stored
beside the originals. These variants check both sides of the margin/border
threshold at additional border widths. No corpus content is used.

The thin variant's previously retained 0.205pt discrepancies (case 8 column 4,
case 10 column 3) no longer reproduce on main 09611f9b. A fresh reference
export on September 29 exactly reproduces all 80 stored x/baseline origins.
The current browser's maximum x error is 0.155005pt and baseline error is
0.010010pt across the twenty cases. Full page pairs 8 and 10 were inspected.
The comparison is now an ordinary passing regression, with the original 0.2pt
threshold and all editing checks retained. It also verifies source/cases/PDF
hashes before using the reference. This records the effect of earlier general
AutoFit corrections; no new layout adjustment or reference replacement is made.
